name: Process similarity
question: How alike are the core processes (order to cash, procure to pay, make to stock or order) across the entities?
score_1: Different business models. Little of the process design could be shared.
score_3: Same broad flow, but real local variants in pricing, planning or fulfilment.
score_5: Effectively the same processes with minor local differences.

name: Commercial case
question: Is there a net benefit over five years after one-off cost, parallel running, licences, support and finance sign-off?
score_1: Negative or not yet built. Benefits are asserted, not measured.
score_3: Positive but small, with payback beyond three years or heavy dependence on one assumption.
score_5: Clearly positive and validated by finance, with payback inside about three years and benefits that survive a pessimistic case.

name: Shared customers, suppliers and parts
question: How much do the entities share customers, suppliers and parts, so that one set of master data would help?
score_3: Some overlap in a few key accounts or part families.
score_5: Large overlap where a single view of the customer, supplier or part is commercially valuable.

name: Group reporting and control pain
question: How much does the current set-up hurt: slow close, manual consolidation, weak intercompany control, audit findings?
score_1: Reporting is timely and controlled with existing tools.
score_3: Noticeable manual effort and some delays, but a reporting layer could cover it.
score_5: Repeated audit findings or a close measured in weeks that a reporting layer would not fix.

name: Contract and licence timing
question: Do contract end dates, support end dates and hardware refresh cycles line up with a migration window?
score_1: Long contracts with exit penalties and no alignment between entities.
score_3: Some alignment, with a window opening in two to three years.
score_5: Contracts or support end within about 18 months, or a platform is already out of support.

name: Strategic stability
question: Is the shape of the group stable enough to justify a long-lived platform decision?
score_1: Entities may be sold, merged or changed materially.
score_3: Broadly stable, with one open question.
score_5: Stable shape and shared direction for the planning horizon.

name: Customisation depth
question: How much custom code, bespoke reports and unusual configuration would have to be rebuilt or retired?
score_1: Heavily customised, poorly documented and central to operations.
score_3: A mix of documented extensions and some undocumented ones.
score_5: Mostly standard functionality and a short list of documented extensions.

name: Regulatory and statutory differences
question: How different are statutory reporting, tax, e-invoicing, language and record retention requirements between the entities?
score_1: Different regimes with local formats or filings the target cannot produce.
score_3: Different countries, but the target covers the requirements with known workarounds.

name: Currency and legal entity complexity
question: How complex are currencies, fiscal calendars, intercompany flows and legal entity structures?
score_1: Many currencies, different year ends and heavy intercompany trading.
score_3: Two currencies or calendars, with manageable intercompany.
score_5: Single currency, same calendar and simple intercompany.

name: Change capacity
question: Do finance, operations and IT have the time and people to deliver this on top of the day job?
score_1: Teams are at their limit, other programmes compete and the window includes year end.
score_3: Some capacity if backfill is funded and other work is sequenced.
score_5: Capacity is ring fenced, backfill is funded and the window is clear.

name: Data quality and master data readiness
question: How clean are the customer, supplier, part and chart of accounts data (see the readiness scorecard)?
score_1: Readiness scorecard shows red results that have no owner or plan.
score_3: Amber results with owners and dates.
score_5: Green or near green, with duplicates and mappings under control.

name: Sponsor and governance strength
question: Is there an accountable executive with authority over every entity, and a funded programme team?
score_1: Nominal sponsor, no dedicated team, decisions escalate slowly.
score_3: Sponsor exists but authority over some entities is partial.
score_5: Board level sponsor with authority over all entities and a funded, named team.

name: Integration and interface footprint
question: How many integrations (banks, EDI, shop floor, warehouse, tax, payroll) must be rebuilt?
score_5: Few integrations, all documented and standard.

name: Local system or statutory books required
question: Does a legal or regulatory requirement oblige any entity in scope to keep a local system, or local statutory books, that the target platform cannot produce?

name: No accountable executive sponsor
question: Is there no executive with authority over every entity in scope who will own the outcome?

name: Sale or restructure expected
question: Is a sale, merger or major restructure of an in-scope entity agreed or likely within twelve months?

name: Target platform unproven
question: Is the target platform still unproven for any in-scope entity's core process, with no working pilot and no comparable reference?
